instantiated_cells.justification: The definition of “lobbyist” is based on being employed/paid by a principal and, for mixed duties, making lobbying communications on each of at least 5 days within a reporting period, not on any minimum payment amount.

A principal anticipating $500 or less in annual lobbying expenditures may file a verified statement and then the principal and its lobbyist are exempt from licensing/registration/reporting, and principals register only after exceeding $500 in a calendar year.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled sections define “lobbyist” by employment/economic consideration and (for mixed duties) a 5-days communications test, but do not set any dollar-amount-of-lobbyist-expenditures threshold that triggers lobbyist status/registration.

The bundled text requires principals (not lobbyists) to file expense statements and includes some internal thresholds (e.g., $200 per-lobbyist listing), but does not contain a lobbyist-filed expenditure reporting requirement to evaluate whether lobbyists must disclose all expenditures or only above a threshold.

The statute contains a 10-hours-per-reporting-period exclusion for certain non-lobbyist employees in principal expense statements, but it does not provide a lobbyist-specific exemption based on a percentage of compensated time devoted to lobbying.
